Fit and evaluate XGBoost regression models on Spark

Source: R/spark.R
fit_xgb_spark.Rd

Reads Parquet data into Spark, assembles numeric predictors, and fits one XGBoost regression model per fold of each resampling repeat. Each native booster is saved as a .ubj file. Out-of-fold predictions are combined into one Parquet dataset, and evaluation metrics and a model index are returned in R.

Usage

fit_xgb_spark(
  master,
  home,
  workspace,
  database = "duckdb",
  input = NULL,
  pred,
  model,
  rset,
  xvar,
  yvar,
  dvar,
  stage = "base",
  ...
)

Arguments

master

character(1). Spark master URL or local master specification, passed to sparklyr::spark_connect().

home

character(1). Spark installation directory, passed as spark_home to sparklyr::spark_connect().

workspace

character(1). Base directory for default Spark paths.

database

character(1). Default database name passed to spark_environment(). Currently retained as configuration metadata only.

input

Character path or paths to input Parquet data, passed to sparklyr::spark_read_parquet(). A usable path must be supplied despite the NULL default. Data must contain site_id, time, lon, lat, the response, and numeric predictor columns.

pred

character(1). Directory for the combined out-of-fold prediction dataset, written with overwrite mode. It must be accessible to Spark and the local R process for returned file discovery.

model

character(1). Directory for native booster files named rset_NNN_fold_NN.ubj. It is created if needed and must be accessible to the Spark driver and later prediction jobs. Keep it separate from pred so overwriting prediction data does not remove saved models.

rset

Nested list of resampling repeats and folds. Each rset[[r]][[f]] must contain analysis and assessment vectors of site_id values used for training and testing, respectively. These are site identifiers, not row positions or rsample split objects.

xvar

Character vector of predictor names. Must be identical, including order, to the numeric columns in the Spark schema after excluding yvar and dvar.

yvar

character(1). Response column name, aliased to label in Spark.

dvar

Character vector of columns excluded from predictor discovery, typically site identifiers and time columns.

stage

character(1). Prefix for prediction columns, which are named using sprintf("%s_%03d", stage, r) for repeat r. Use "base" or "meta" to distinguish the two learner stages.

...

Reserved for future use. Currently ignored.

Value

A list with:

  • pred: character vector of .parquet paths beneath pred that were not present before writing. Paths with unchanged names are excluded.

  • eval: data frame with rset and fold identifiers, metric and value columns for RMSE, MSE, R-squared, and MAE, and time, the elapsed fitting time in seconds repeated for each metric within a fold.

  • model: list containing index, a data frame with integer rset and fold, character prediction, and absolute native-booster path columns; xvar, the ordered predictor names; yvar, the response name; and stage, the prediction prefix. The caller can save this list for later reuse.

Details

Requires the sparklyr and DBI packages, a working Spark installation, and compatible XGBoost4J-Spark JARs. A nonempty XGBOOST_JARS environment variable supplies JAR paths through sparklyr.shell.jars; otherwise the Maven coordinate from spark_environment() is used. See that helper for resource limits, boosting rounds, seed, warehouse path, and row-limit settings. A positive row limit uses SQL LIMIT without an ordering clause.

Models use CPU histogram training with squared-error loss, maximum depth 8, learning rate 0.1, and row and column sampling fractions of 0.8. Feature vectors are made dense so zero values remain explicit. Each fold's native booster is saved immediately after fitting, before held-out prediction. The Spark connection is disconnected on exit, including on error.

Within each repeat, held-out predictions are row-bound across folds. Repeats are then left-joined by site_id and time, retaining identifiers and the response from the first repeat. The dataset beneath pred contains site_id, time, lon, lat, the response under its original name, and one prediction column per repeat. It can contain multiple Parquet part files.

The returned model metadata retains the predictor order and maps each repeat and fold to its saved booster path and prediction-column name. Pass this complete model list to predict_xgb_spark() for subsequent prediction.

See also

spark_environment(), assemble_xgb_features(), predict_xgb_spark()
